title: Canonical benchmark is the combined ON versus OFF cost bounded agentic bench
summary: Decision 2026-06-18: the single canonical Zonoid benchmark going forward is the combined ON-vs-OFF cost-bounded agentic bench (extends scripts/bench-economy.js). ON runs production parity (full KB + DAG) and we measure BOTH accuracy (held-out grader) and token spend; OFF runs pure agentic in a clean no-memory environment with budget cap = ON's measured spend; per problem we record whether OFF can match ON's outcome within ON's cost. DROP the old standalone benches: the single-shot feature QA bench (bench/zonoid_bench) is partially contaminated (cold arm scored 58.9 percent on the LLM-judge rescore) and structurally cannot measure token economy because injecting context makes ON cost MORE per call; the conversational LOCOMO / LongMemEval harness (bench/agent-memory) targets the wrong capability and rests on disputed vendor self-claims (Zep 84 to 58.44 to 75.14 LoCoMo dispute; Mem0's own paper shows a full-context baseline beating its memory). KEEP bench/economy and scripts/bench-economy.js — they are the FOUNDATION of the combined bench, not part of the old set. The feature bench's memory-dependent probes (decision and gotcha categories, which showed a clean +32 to +33 point lift) are mined as SOURCE MATERIAL for new roughly 500k-scale agentic scenarios. ON has no token budget today — only a shared wall-clock timeout — so problem size is the lever for scaling ON spend, not a config knob.
